scope: Development evidence only: the first native aarch64 bulk build of the Daemonarchy image package closure, an unsigned aarch64 package feed, and an unsigned aarch64 UEFI installer ISO with a QEMU/EDK2 boot to the installer menu. Nothing here is signed, published, admitted to the release graph or produced under LitAI custody. No install, upgrade, rollback, desktop or debugging case was run, and nothing qualifies aarch64.
signing: None. No signing key was present or used. The feed was made with pkg repo without a key, build-iso.sh ran without PACKAGE_REPOSITORY_PUBLIC_KEY or Secure Boot inputs, and neither artifact carries a signature.

worker.swap: 2 GiB partition. A temporary 16 GiB swap zvol was added for run 1 and destroyed after the host-disk incident at the operator's direction.
worker.disk: VMware Virtual NVMe, 200 GiB. nvmecontrol identify reports Dataset Management Command: Not Supported, so ZFS TRIM cannot return freed blocks to a thin-provisioned host disk.

pool_allocation.after_run1_reboot: 25.8G (zpool list, after the reboot; the 16G swap zvol was then destroyed)
pool_allocation.note: The allocation guard sampled every 120 s from run 2 on, against the operator's 150G stop limit; the peak was 54380019712 bytes (50.6 GiB). After the ISO: packages 6.8G, distfiles 5.3G, unsigned feed 1.5G, images 1.5G, bulk logs 73M. The disk has no TRIM, so the host-side size of a thin VMDK may exceed the pool allocation.

worker.host_incident: Run 1 was killed at about 2026-10-26T22:00Z when the VMware host ran out of disk and the worker rebooted. This was not a guest fault. zroot came back healthy (zpool status -x clean). poudriere jail -k removed the stale .m reference mounts. Every completed package survived in .building (1144 entries) and run 2 resumed from it. No evidence was lost: the smoke ISO, its serial logs and the release sets were already on disk.

failures.phase: build (pre-build: npm run build of the Svelte/Vite frontend)
failures.diagnosis: The port builds its frontend offline from aether-4.30.0-npm-cache.tar.gz. That cache holds only the FreeBSD x64 builds of @rolldown/binding, lightningcss and @tailwindcss/oxide. npm publishes no FreeBSD arm64 build of any of the three (registry 404 on 2026-10-27). rolldown and tailwind oxide have wasm32-wasi builds; lightningcss has none in its node package.
failures.disposition: Gap. ports#30 drops aether from x11-wm/daemonarchy's aarch64 dependencies. A real fix needs a new distfile: either a prebuilt, architecture-independent frontend/dist from the pinned source and lockfile, or an npm cache with WASI bindings plus a lightningcss replacement. Publishing either distfile is an operator action. Generating the frontend outside poudriere was not attempted.

A keypress did not reach it because this machine had no keyboard device.

boot2.result: The same with qemu-xhci and usb-kbd. Return opened the installer options menu: Install Daemonarchy, Remote agent debug, Configure network, Exit to shell. The run was stopped there.

boot_evidence.finding_vtnet_witness: On both boots, bringing up vtnet0 logs WITNESS warnings and a lock order reversal (50 'VTNET Core Lock' lines in boot 1, 52 in boot 2). vtnet_init_locked -> vtnet_set_macaddr (if_vtnet.c:1570) calls bus_dmamap_create while holding the vtnet core mutex. On arm64 that reaches bounce_bus_dmamap_create -> alloc_bounce_zone, which mallocs, adds a sysctl (sysctl lock, sleepable rm) and kproc_creates. Boot and DHCP continue. The smoke ISO, whose rc.conf configures no interface address, shows none of this. Not diagnosed further: it belongs to daemonarchy-src or upstream if_vtnet, and is not yet compared with amd64.
boot_evidence.not_run: No install to the target disk: the installer would fetch from the packages-16-aarch64 feed, which is not published. No upgrade, rollback, desktop (no KMS driver; gap 2) or network-debugging case. VMware arm64 guests were not used for the image.

The images are in /usr/local/poudriere/data/images/ and the feed in /usr/local/poudriere/data/daemonarchy-repo/packages-16-aarch64-dev20261027/. None of them is published.
